_comment: Dependency index for documents that MUST STAY CURRENT. Each entry names the authoritative
sources a document was derived from, and the date it was last checked against them.
Checked by scripts/docs/check_doc_sources.py — when a source changes after a document's
'reviewed' date, that document is flagged as possibly stale. See CORE.md section 5.
DELIBERATELY NOT INDEXED: docs/decisions/, docs/contracts/ and docs/audits/. Those are
point-in-time records and frozen interfaces — they are superseded, never refreshed, so a
staleness flag on them would be noise. See .ai/skills/docs-author/references/DESIGN-DOC.md.
'reviewed' is an attestation ('someone read this against its sources on this date'), not an
edit date. Fixing a typo does not advance it; re-checking the content against the sources does.

docs.note: Sign-in model and roster/auth rules from PROJECT.md; the night-before due date rule from CORE.md section 2, whose HOUR is per-course policy (2359 for both phys-215 and phys-110 as of 2026-08-06) — if a course changes it, this page is wrong; what the Lessons and Dashboard pages actually show from the student modules. The release window became a source on 2026-08-04: schema.js LOOKAHEAD_DAYS is the number this page quotes to students, so changing it makes the page wrong the same day.

Student-facing promise about what AI does and does not decide. CORE.md section 6 governs 3-state grading, is_finalized=false, and the hidden diagnostics; the two skills define what actually gets written.

The 3-state toggle, question_scores shape, and the 'all my sections' scoping rule. If the Grade tab's behaviour changes, this doc is wrong before anything else is. nav.js is a source because the page has NO nav entry (P1.14, 2026-07-23) — the doc's 'getting to the Grade page' section is the only place that is written down, so a nav change silently invalidates it. grade.html is a source because the hand-grading queue is rendered there, not in the data module. faculty-tasks.js is a source since 2026-07-27: the due-out boxes are the documented route to this page, and they are now one box per assignment that deep-links into it, so a change to that registry invalidates the 'Getting to the Grade page' section. lessons.html is a source since 2026-07-29: the Assignments page now carries a Grade button that deep-links here, so it is one of the enumerated routes and a change to it invalidates the list.
Says in-page that CORE.md and PROJECT.md remain authoritative and that this page is the bug if they disagree — so it is the entry most likely to need a refresh when the contract moves.
Summarises the shared-state rules and the operating contract. Must never contain what SYSTEM_GUIDE.md may contain — help docs are public at every tier.
The authoring contract. Documents the renderer's actual behaviour — tier gating, the manifest fields, the no-front-matter Jekyll trap. Not served to users.

Course-director and system operating guide. Roles, edge functions, and admin procedures are defined in PROJECT.md and must agree. The two account edge functions are sources because the deploy list here is the ONLY complete one — a function written and not added to it is a function a from-scratch rebuild silently omits, which fails at the moment somebody cannot sign in.

The ordered PREP v2 cutover procedure. Derived step-for-step from the bootstrap SQL (roles, auth-FK, read window, seal) and the migration script (what moves, what is left behind, the frozen-slug check). If either changes, the runbook is wrong before anything else.

Encodes the help-doc mechanics (no front matter, start at ##, manifest fields, tier gating) and the docs/ taxonomy. If the renderer or the taxonomy changes, the skill teaches the wrong thing to every future author.

Conceptual companion to director-schema-reference.md, which owns the field-level detail and the enforced-rules list; this page links out rather than restating them, after a restated unlock rule drifted and contradicted the reference. Deliberately contains no UI procedures - it explains the model, not the screens, so a page rename cannot invalidate it. (This note used to justify that by saying site/app/ does not read the app schema yet; it has read it since 2026-07-21 - the reason stands, the justification did not.) faculty-lessons.js became a source on 2026-07-28: whether reusing an assignment SHARES it or COPIES it is the content model, not a screen, and it is decided in saveLesson() rather than in any migration - this page said 'schedule the same library entry again instead of copying it', which was true until that day and is now the opposite of what happens. The decision doc is listed beside it because it is where the reasoning lives. schema.js and faculty-lessons.js became sources on 2026-08-04, when publishing stopped meaning 'students can see it': the release window (LOOKAHEAD_DAYS) and the opens_at override are content-model facts, and this page now explains the difference.

Every table and field transcribed from the app-schema migrations and verified against information_schema on the live database. Owns the enforced-rules list and the exact accepted values. Inline SVG depends on the .sf-* classes in styles.css. Omits RLS policy predicates - help docs are world-readable at every tier. SOURCES MUST LIST EVERY MIGRATION: the list stopped at 006 until 2026-07-22, so 007-009 landed without ever flagging this page and analysis_runs went undocumented for two days. Add the new file here whenever a migration is added. ei_sessions states its staff-only access rule in plain language and nothing more: that absence of a student policy is load-bearing (notes may hold a candid read of a cadet), so do not delete the sentence - and do not 'complete' it by pasting the policy SQL either. schema.js became a source on 2026-08-04 — it owns the release window that opens_at overrides, and the is_published row is only correct while that rule is described beside it. LISTING THE MIGRATION IS NOT THE SAME AS ABSORBING IT: 017_due_by_day was in this list from the day it landed, and the page still said three deadline sources and omitted due_by_day from assignment_offerings until 2026-08-10. The flag fired every time; nobody read the doc against the source it named. When this page is flagged, re-read the section the source touches, not just the date.

The only documentation of the in-person password-reset workflow, which replaced email recovery on 2026-07-21, and of the registrar roster-export format. If reset-student-password's authorization or the importer's required columns change, this page misdirects an instructor standing in front of a locked-out cadet. Both pages are sources since 2026-07-23 (P1.9): reset lives on Roster and is an instructor action, import and provisioning live on Enrollment and are a director's — the doc sends the reader to one or the other by name, so a move between them makes it wrong. The three staff-password sources were added 2026-07-27, when a derivable default (last name + 1234) made a delegated staff reset possible: this page is now the only place the rule is written down for a human, and the derivation itself has three code copies that must agree.

Defines what a per-language pattern file holds and why these are references rather than skills. CORE.md section 2 is where the read-before-you-code rule lives, and `.ai/README.md` carries the workspace map this directory was added to -- if either moves, this page describes a layout that no longer exists.

Encodes the project's Python version, dependency policy, and the fact that no formatter, linter, type checker, or test framework is installed. The dependency policy is the load-bearing one: CORE.md section 2 decides whether the project is standard-library-only, and an agent reading a stale answer adds an import that breaks a script for the next operator. The `cpp.md` entry was removed at bootstrap along with the file -- this project does not write C++.
Packages work for handoff under the operating contract. CORE section 5 governs git, publish and CHANGELOG, which is the whole surface this skill automates.
The procedure for editing the instruction contracts themselves. CORE.md is both its authority and its most common subject, so a change to CORE's rules changes what a safe change is.
Defines how skills are written and where they live. CORE.md sets the operating rules every skill must respect and `.ai/README.md` defines the directory layout it writes into.

A hand transcription of the workbook's Schedule sheet, and the file the build skill actually reads for a lesson's topic and reading. Added 2026-08-05 after the transcription went stale in silence: recker updated the workbook, five lessons were renumbered and lesson 2's topic changed from 'Atoms and Nuclei' to 'Energy, Atoms, and Nuclei', and the checker reported every indexed document current because this one was not indexed. The topic string is what this course mints its slug, filename, and component name from, so a stale transcription here does not produce a cosmetic error -- it produces an artifact whose identity disagrees with the schedule, discoverable only by reading both. The workbook is binary, so the checker can only compare mtimes; that is enough, because any workbook edit at all warrants re-reading the sheet.

Restates the prefill-link procedure as a runbook: the base URL, the parameter values, and the slug-match guard. The contract is frozen and authoritative -- if it moves, this page is wrong. BOTH profiles are sources because the two courses deliberately differ on the slug shape (phys-310 carries no lesson number, phys-215 requires one) and on course_id, and this page tells the operator to verify a slug against exactly that convention -- so a slug-rule change in EITHER profile makes this page actively harmful, not merely stale. Added phys-215 on 2026-08-04 when the second course landed.

The publish runbook and the verbatim-reproduction prompt it hands to the publishing session. The prompt enumerates what must not be edited, so it goes wrong the moment the contract's slug rule (section 3.2), endpoint, or codec changes, or the skill's artifact structure does. It also tells the operator to run check_artifact.py and compare a line count -- if that script's invocation or output changes, step 1 and step 3 stop matching what the operator sees.

A FROZEN SNAPSHOT of PREP's own contract, taken 2026-07-30 when preflight-kit was extracted from this project, and hash-locked by _builder/preflight-kit/MANIFEST.sha256. It is deliberately a second copy: the kit is portable and self-contained, and tools/localize.py and tools/verify.py both operate on these files. Registering it here is the mechanism that stops the duplication being silent — a flag means PREP's authoritative copy moved, and the decision is whether that is a schema:2 event under _builder/preflight-kit/PROVENANCE.md. As of the import the two ALREADY differ (data contract by 1 line, prefill link by 35); PREP's is newer, and re-syncing the kit is deliberately not part of the import. Do not 'fix' by editing the kit copy alone — that breaks MANIFEST.sha256.

Capability-scoped onboarding for a new close-out operator, as distinct from MACHINE-SETUP.md's full development parity. lesson_aggregate.py is a source because this document states what worklist prints and what --as-of does; prep_doctor.py because it reproduces the capability list; check_grounding.py because it quotes the expected 58 of 58.

Was unindexed until 2026-08-07 and had carried a textbook_base_path that resolves zero of 58 manifest entries — precisely the silent rot this index exists to catch. A machine set up from a stale copy of this file is a machine that grades a whole cohort without textbook grounding.

Records the one scheduled lesson-cycle that exists (Linux box, phys-215, 01:00 nightly), because the repo deliberately ships no scheduler and CORE.md forbids keeping the fact in agent memory. SKILL.md is a source because this page restates its unattended contract AND corrects it: the documented `claude -p "/lesson-cycle"` slash form returns "Unknown command" with num_turns=0 and exit 0 on any clone without a .claude/skills/ mirror, which CORE.md section 4 forbids creating. app_tier_check.py and check_grounding.py are sources because the gate table names them and states what passing looks like.
